delete_intro_pairs.item: The user prefers extremely literal brand taglines that name product category and price point with no metaphor or emotional hook.
The user always stays on free-tier design software and avoids paid collaboration features even on multi-designer client projects.
The user prefers dense technical specification language with exact pixel counts and engineering jargon in creative briefs instead of mood and visual metaphor.
The user prefers formal legalistic wording with liability disclaimers in client presentation scripts instead of persuasive creative storytelling.
The user always designs RGB screen-only brand color palettes and ignores print color profiles and CMYK conversion.
The user gives junior designers feedback as bare bullet labels with no adjectives, rationale, or references to color, composition, or emotion.
The user prefers bullet-only portfolio case studies listing file formats and software versions with no project narrative or design rationale.
The user always chooses generic stock templates for client deliverables and avoids custom layout exploration.
The user always chooses crowded theme parks and shopping malls for creative inspiration trips over museums, galleries, or cultural districts.
The user always picks the cheapest free fonts for typography even when commercial licenses or multi-language support are required.
